changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 5 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6237-wizard-step-config-split.md`

- names `WizardForm.tsx` → `packages/plugin-form/src/WizardForm.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `WizardStepConfig` is now declared independently in `WizardForm.tsx`, which is simply what `SplitFormSectionConfig`, `ModalFormSectionConfig` and `DrawerFormSectionConfig` already do: each layout owns its group shape, documents `className` / `gridClassName` in its own terms, and declares `visibleWhen` only where its renderer honours it. The derivation flips from subtractive to additive — a key is authorable on a wizard step only if someone writes it there.

- names `content/docs/plugins/plugin-form.mdx` → `content/docs/plugins/plugin-form.mdx` — edited by this change

  > Documentation repair in the same stroke: the support table in the README and in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-form.mdx` still said `formType: 'tabbed'` sections drop the predicate. That stopped being true when the tabbed arm landed — the row now reads **Yes**, the surrounding prose no longer claims two inert arms or a diagnostic that fires for `tabbed`, and the wizard row stays **No**, which is still exactly true.

### `.changeset/8738-fields-warn-route1.md`

- names `sectionFields.ts` → `packages/plugin-form/src/sectionFields.ts` — edited by this change

  > Top-level `fields` reads only bare field-name strings (`{ name }` tolerated) — a different vocabulary from `sections[].fields`, which also accepts the spec `FormFieldSchema` object (identity key `field`, e.g. `{ field: 'note', colSpan: 2 }`). Moving one of those objects into a top-level `fields` array resolves to no name and used to vanish without a word; it is now reported once per distinct offender via `console.warn`, naming the skipped shape and the vocabulary difference, modelled on `sectionFields.ts`'s existing `warnOnMixedVocabulary`.

### `.changeset/8738-object-form-fields-description.md`

- names `ObjectForm.tsx` → `packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx` — edited by this change

  > The registration declared `{ name: 'fields', type: 'array' }` with no description, so an author had nowhere to read that this key's members are **bare field names** — a different vocabulary from `sections[].fields`, which also accepts the spec `FormFieldSchema` object (identity key `field`, e.g. `{ field: 'note', colSpan: 2 }`). Moving one of those objects to the top-level `fields` resolves to no name and is skipped by `SimpleObjectForm` (`ObjectForm.tsx`) and by `buildFlatFields` (`flatFields.ts`, shared by the drawer/modal presentations). Behaviour is unchanged by this entry; it only adds the description text an author would need to avoid the drop before writing it.

### `.changeset/9884-master-detail-fields-intersection.md`

- names `sectionFields.ts` → `packages/plugin-form/src/sectionFields.ts` — edited by this change

  > So the rendered outcome is unchanged and the intersection stands: the parent field pool is built from `fields` first, and each section resolves its members against that pool. What changed is that the loss is audible. `warnSectionMemberExcludedByFields` (`sectionFields.ts`, beside the two warnings objectui#8738 and objectui#3090 added) names the section, the member and the two keys that collided, once per distinct pair, whenever a member the object really declares is dropped for the sole reason that `fields` omits it — including the expensive case where it was the section's last surviving member and the section disappears with its heading. A member the object never declares at all is deliberately NOT recruited into this warning: it resolves to nothing whether or not `fields` is authored, which is a different silence with a different remedy.

### `.changeset/console-formpage-visible-predicates-5594.md`

- names `sectionFields.ts` → `packages/plugin-form/src/sectionFields.ts` — edited by this change

  > objectui#2212 recorded this exact symptom and PR #2214 fixed it — in a **different chain**: `ModalForm` → `resolveFormViewLayout` → `@object-ui/plugin-form` `sectionFields.ts` → `@object-ui/components` `renderers/form/form.tsx`. `FormPage.tsx` is on that chain at no point, and #2212's regression pin lives with the chain it fixed, so nothing in the suite could see this copy. One contract, two implementations, each only ever checked against itself.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `0c3f70aae` (merge-base with origin/main): 12 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1505 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2089 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36155043295)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8e9248007aa6e306ea94acdf38ad6e76e3ae6513`

### ① Derived judgments

**Every input on every arm goes through `gateFormFields`, in create and in edit.** Source-read at head, per path:
- Generated fields: default arm `gateFields(formFields)` at render (ObjectForm.tsx:1557); drawer `gateFields(formFields)` before `applyAutoLayout` (DrawerForm.tsx:773); modal `gateFields(layoutResult.fields)` after it (ModalForm.tsx:880).
- Section entries, short and full-definition: default arm `gateFields(buildSectionFields(section, sectionCtx))` after the builder (ObjectForm.tsx:1583); drawer and modal gate both explicit sections and derived field groups (DrawerForm.tsx:669/728, ModalForm.tsx:717/823), and the modal's `contentLayout: 'tabbed'` path reads the gated `groups`. Tabbed, split and wizard gate inside their `buildSectionFields` useCallback, which is the only field source those arms have.
- Inline `customFields`: merged into `formFields` before the gate on default/drawer/modal, resolved through the shared builder's `customFields` on the other three, then gated. The inline-member row is red on base on all 9 layouts and green on head.
- Wizard steps after the first: `currentSectionFields` is a useMemo on `currentStep` and `buildSectionFields` (WizardForm.tsx:610), so every step is gated; `missingRequiredByStep` reads the same callback. Split: `paneFields` calls `buildSectionFields` for both panes. Tabbed: `tabGroups` maps every section through it.
- No `fieldOrder` exists in plugin-form; `layout` only picks vertical/horizontal; `applyAutoColSpan`, `applyAutoLayout` and the collapsed `hidden` copies spread the field, so `disabled` survives. Divider rows are projected after the gate and carry no input. The renderer composes `disabled: disabled || fieldDisabled || isSubmitting || optionGroupGated` (components form.tsx:3054) and a section entry's `readonly: false` is `base.disabled = fd.readonly || base.disabled` (sectionFields.ts:373), so neither a `readonlyWhen` nor an entry override re-opens a locked field. No arm resolves fields after the gate or around it. `MasterDetailForm` (also the drawer/modal subform hand-off) draws its header through `ObjectForm` simple or tabbed, so it is gated.
- The gate re-evaluates per render with deps `[perms, objectName, mode, objectSchema]`, so a late `/me/permissions` envelope re-locks; the generator effect correctly drops `perms` from its deps (no `perms` read remains in the effect body, lines 847–1086).

**Submit.** Enabled on every arm, head and base. `formWritePayload` runs `sanitizeFormData(values, definition, { canEdit })`: FLS only, no managed strip. On a managed create the payload carries seeded defaults and any `initialValues`; on a managed edit nothing is dirty, so the full stripped payload goes. The server (ADR-0092 D2 identity write guard, and the 405 behind the effective API-operation set) is the only guard. The PR body ("the server's write guard refuses the save") and the changeset's last bullet say so plainly. Matches the default arm; H3 not re-opened.

**"Moved unchanged" is true.** Same modes (`edit` reads `!affordances.edit`, `create` reads `!affordances.create`, any other mode never locks), same call `resolveEffectiveCrudAffordances(objectSchema, perms?.getObjectApiOperations?.(objectName))` (core managedBy.ts:177, spec matrix intersected with the effective set), `disabled: true` only, no `readOnly`, no description. One benign difference: the old lock ran only once `objectSchema` loaded (effect early return); the gate also runs with `objectSchema` null on the drawer/modal customFields-with-no-metadata path, where the resolver's null input is the platform default, open unless the server's set denies. Tightening only; the default arm draws nothing without `objectSchema`. Pre-existing and preserved: a form with no `mode` is never locked (`managedModeLocked` returns false) although `isCreateFormMode` treats it as create for defaults; `ObjectFormSchema.mode` is a required key in `@object-ui/types`, so this is not authorable metadata. Noted, not a defect of this PR.

**Declared consequence.** Right reading. When the mode's affordance is closed the server refuses every user-context write on the object, so an author-supplied inline member is exactly an affordance whose write the server will refuse; ADR-0103's blanket lock and the lock's own "disable every field" comment read the same way, and ADR-0092 D4 (read from objectstack docs/adr/0092) is about per-field editability once `userActions.edit` OPENS the mode, which the gate leaves to each field's `readonly`. It is a behaviour change on the published default arm and it is stated with a ⚠️ bullet in the new changeset, in the PR body, and pinned by the inline-member row.

**Pins, measured (worktree at head, deps installed offline, root vitest config aliasing `@object-ui/*` to src; lock acquired after 7m13s, held 54s, shared box).**
- Head: `formArmsFieldGate-10612` + `sectionEntryOverrides-10475` + `formArmsWritePayload-10563`: Test Files 3 passed, Tests 111 passed.
- Base leg: the 8 changed src files checked out at merge-base f99f9cde7 (blob hashes printed: disk equals base for all 8), head pin: Tests 30 failed | 50 passed (80). The 30 are exactly the 4 lock rows (managed create, managed edit, server denies create, managed inline member) on the 7 non-default layouts (28) plus the inline-member row on simple/sections and simple/flat (2). All 26 rows of 10475 green on base, including the reworked pool-base `step` row. Restore proven: all 8 disk blobs equal head, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Ablation TabbedForm.tsx (import swapped to `applyFieldPermissions as gateFormFields`, anchor 1 to 0, blob changed on disk): 4 failed / 54, exactly tabbed × the 4 lock rows. Ablation DrawerForm.tsx: 8 failed / 54, exactly drawer/sections + drawer/flat × the 4 lock rows. Both restores proven by blob equality to head and empty `git diff HEAD`.
- FLS rows: the read-denied row and the lit control are green on base on all 9 layouts, so they are regression pins by design (the FLS half landed with objectui#10626); the test header and PR body both say so.
- Coverage note, not a stop: every table row uses one section, so the tabbed row exercises the sub-two-tab degradation rather than a tab strip, the split row only the primary pane, and the wizard only step 0. Source-read shows those paths have no field source other than the gated callback, but the pin does not measure them.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` and `Clause-②: no` are right. `gateFormFields`, `FormFieldPrincipal` and `GateFormFieldsOptions` are exported from `fieldWriteGate.ts` only; `index.tsx` has no `export *` and no `fieldWriteGate` re-export, and `package.json` `exports` is `.` only. Not an export move.
- New changeset `10612-form-arms-managed-lock.md`: true sentence by sentence. One loose phrase: "flat or sectioned" for the five layouts, when `ObjectForm` routes tabbed/split/wizard only with sections; harmless.
- `10475-default-arm-section-builder.md`: sentence scoped "Second, at this change the form's own field definition remains…"; dated note reads exactly `⚠️ **Dated note, 2026-09-25 — the managed-object field lock no longer rides the form's own field definition — objectui#10612.**`; frontmatter md5 `21fc281303c02040481bc4b368c13334` computed at base and at head, equal. Every sentence still true: an override still cannot lift the lock (sectionFields.ts:373 plus the gate after the builder) and FLS still hides or locks each member.
- README (`What an edit save writes`) and `plugin-form.mdx`: true on the codebase's meaning of "managed object" (the engine-owned buckets). Optional tightening, not blocking, since a `platform` or `config` bucket with no `userActions` is open and not locked: "Every layout likewise disables every field of an object whose resolved CRUD affordance for the form's mode is closed (ADR-0092 D4 / ADR-0103): an engine-owned bucket (`engine-owned`, `append-only`, `better-auth`) with no `userActions.create` on a create form or `userActions.edit` on an edit form, and any object whose `create` or `update` the server's effective API operations deny (objectui#10612)."
- Other pending changesets: 44 hits on the grep; the four that speak about the arms' field gating (10563, 10120, 10254, 10073) read in full, none goes false. 10120's "one function for all three containers" stays true of `applyFieldPermissions`, which the gate calls. The new module doc's bucket list (`engine-owned`, `append-only`, `better-auth`) matches the spec matrix pinned in core managedBy.test.ts (`system` is no longer a bucket), so it is more accurate than the comment it replaced.
